literal: Hostility called grievous disease if removed, failing without, decay without glory it will give.
translation: If one removes the grievous disease called hostility, it will yield unfailing and undecaying glory.
modern: இகல் என்று சொல்லப்படும் துன்பம் தரும் நோயை ஒருவன் தன் மனதிலிருந்து நீக்கிவிட்டால், அது அவனுக்கு அழிவில்லாத நிலையான புகழைத் தரும்.
explanation: This couplet describes hostility as a grievous disease that afflicts the mind. The word 'இகல்' (hostility or enmity) is paired with 'எவ்வ நோய்' (grievous disease) to emphasize how destructive it is to one's own well-being. If a person can completely remove this disease, the very act of curing themselves of hatred will grant them 'விளக்கம்' (glory or brightness) that is both 'தவல் இல்லா' (unfailing) and 'தா இல்' (undecaying). Thus, letting go of enmity is presented not just as a moral good, but as the ultimate path to lasting greatness.
